doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Recording for Nagel-Heyer
summary: His German label releases one or two records a year and promotes them well.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What’s it like trying to find outlets for recording these days? You get hooked up with a good label and try to stay with them?
Exactly. I’m lucked into a wonderful situation with a label in Germany.

Nagel-Heyer, yeah. And they have been wonderful to me. I do between one and two records a year for them. They promote my records, they do all they can, they spend a lot of money in advertising, they hired Allegro Distribution to distribute the records all through so they’re now like in Borders bookstores and Sound Warehouse and Tower Records and all these places. I mean I can’t say enough good things about them, they are the sweetest, nicest people in the world, and they are just trying to promote good music on records and have done a wonderful job.

And there again, they’re trying to record the entire spectrum of the music. They just did a great thing with Wycliffe Gordon, and they have no prejudices. They like good musicians and good music. Again I can’t say enough good things — it’s another thing that I consider myself a very lucky person to have met them.
